{{Short description|Cypriot theoretical physicist (1952–2022)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2023}}
'''Costas Christou Kounnas''' (Κώστας Χρήστου Κουννάς, 23 January 1952 – 21 January 2022)<ref name=FamagustaNews>{{cite news|url=https://en.famagusta.news/news/kypros/apeviose-o-ammochostianos-kostas-chr-kounnas-ypirxe-melos-tou-cern/|title=Famagusta resident Costas Chr. Kounnas - He was a member of CERN|newspaper=Famagusta News|date=28 January 2022}}</ref> was a Cypriot theoretical physicist, known for his research on [[string theory]], [[supersymmetry]], [[supergravity]], [[Grand Unified Theory|GUT]]s, and [[quantum chromodynamics]].<ref name=EISA>{{cite news|title=Costas Kounnas (obituary notice)|newspaper=News, European Institute for Sciences and their Applications (EISA)|date=22 January 2022|url=https://www.eisa.institute/news.html}}</ref>

==Biography==
Kounnas born in [[Famagusta]]. After graduating in 1969 from Famagusta's Greek High School for Boys, he graduated with honors from the School of Physics and Mathematics of the [[University of Athens]]. With a scholarship from the French government, he became in 1975 a graduate student at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|ENS Paris]],<ref name=FamagustaNews/> where he received his doctorate in 1981.<ref name=GreekReporter>{{cite news|url=https://greece.greekreporter.com/2014/02/20/cypriot-physicist-wins-humbolt-research-award/|author=Ziakakou, Ioanna|title=Cypriot Physicist Wins Humbolt Research Award|newspaper=Greek Reporter|date=20 February 2014}}</ref> While studying in Paris he married the Famagusta-native Kakia Alexandrou. The couple's son is Christian Kounnas.<ref name=FamagustaNews/>

Costas Kounnas then worked at [[CERN]] (1982 to 1984) and the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1984 to 1987) before returning to the ENS in 1987 as Research Director of the [[CNRS]]. From 1992 to 1999 he was a staff member in the Theory Division of CERN.<ref name=FamagustaNews/><ref name=LangevinPrize>{{cite news|title=Langevin prize|newspaper=CERN Courier|date=November 1995|page=23|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1732474/files/vol35-issue8-p023-e.pdf}}</ref>

He was a visiting professor at [[Stanford University]], the University of California at Los Angeles (UCLA), and [[Harvard University]].<ref name=FamagustaNews/>

In 1987, with [[Ignatios Antoniadis]] and Constantin Bachas, he developed superstring models in four dimensions. Their research initiated much further research in string theory.<ref name=EISA/><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Antoniadis | first1=I. | last2=Bachas | first2=C.P. | last3=Kounnas | first3=C. | title=Four-dimensional superstrings | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=289 | year=1987 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(87)90372-5 | pages=87–108| bibcode=1987NuPhB.289...87A | url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/175165 }}</ref> He was involved in elucidating the properties of supergravity and their influence on and relationship to string theory. He also worked on string cosmology.<ref name=EISA/>

Kounnas received in 1995 the [[Paul Langevin Prize]]<ref name=LangevinPrize/> and in 2013 the [[Gay-Lussac-Humboldt Prize]]. He received a [[Humboldt Research Award]] for the academic year 2014–2015,<ref name=EISA/><ref name=GreekReporter/> during which he collaborated with [[Dieter Lüst]] at [[LMU Munich]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Costas Kounnas, Humboldt prize winner|website=Mathematical Physics and String Theory, Arnold Sommerfeld Institute, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU)|url=https://www.theorie.physik.uni-muenchen.de/MATH/members/former_mem/former_asc/kounnas/index.html}}</ref>

Over many years, Kounnas made important contributions to establishing and developing  the scientific meetings at EISA's Corfu Summer Institute.<ref name=EISA/><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Anagnostopoulos | first1=Konstantinos | last2=Antoniadis | first2=Ignatios | last3=Fanourakis | first3=George | last4=Kehagias | first4=Alexandros | last5=Savoy-Navarro | first5=Aurore | last6=Wess | first6=Julius | last7=Zoupanos | first7=George | title=Corfu Summer Institute on Elementary Particle Physics (CORFU2005) | journal=Journal of Physics: Conference Series | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=53 | date=1 December 2006 | issn=1742-6596 | doi=10.1088/1742-6596/53/1/e01 | s2cid=250685909 | doi-access=free }} (See [[Corfu]].)</ref>

== Selected publications ==
*with E. G. Floratos, R. Lacaze: ''Higher order QCD effects in inclusive annihilation and deep inelastic scattering,'' Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 192, 1981, pp.&nbsp;417–462 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(81)90434-X}} (over 400 citations)
*with [[Eugène Cremmer]], [[Sergio Ferrara]], [[Dimitri Nanopoulos]]: ''Naturally vanishing cosmological constant in N= 1 supergravity'', Phys. Lett. B, vol. 133, 1983, pp.&nbsp;61–66 {{doi|10.1016/0370-2693(83)90106-5}} (over 1000 citations)
*with [[John Ellis (physicist, born 1946)|John Ellis]], D. V. Nanopoulos: ''No-scale supersymmetric GUTs'', Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 247, 1984, pp.&nbsp;373–395 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(84)90555-8}} (over 650 citations)
*with J. Ellis, D. V. Nanopoulos: ''Phenomenological SU (1, 1) supergravity'', Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 241, 1984, pp.&nbsp;406–428 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(84)90054-3}} (over 500 citations)
*with A. B. Lahanas, D. V. Nanopoulos, M. Quirós: ''Low-energy behaviour of realistic locally-supersymmetric grand unified theories'', Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 236, 1984, pp.&nbsp;438–466 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(84)90545-5}} (over 450 citations)
*with E. Cremmer, A. Van Proeyen, J. P. Derendinger, S. Ferrara: B. de Wit, L. Girardello: ''Vector multiplets coupled to N= 2 supergravity: super-Higgs effect, flat potentials and geometric structure,'' Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 250, 1985, pp.&nbsp;385–426 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(85)90488-2}} (over 400 citations)
*with S. Ferrara, M. Porrati: ''General dimensional reduction of ten-dimensional supergravity and superstring'', Phys. Lett. B, vol. 181, 1986, pp.&nbsp;263–268 {{doi|10.1016/0370-2693(86)90043-2}}
*with [[Ignatios Antoniadis|I. Antoniadis]], C. Bachas: ''Four-dimensional Superstrings''. In: ''Nucl. Phys. B'', vol. 289, 1987, pp.&nbsp;87–108 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(87)90372-5}} (over 1000 citations)
*mit M. Porrati: ''Spontaneous supersymmetry breaking in string theory'', Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 310, 1988, pp.&nbsp;355–370 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(88)90153-8}} (over 300 citations)
*with S. Ferrara, M. Porrati, F. Zwirner: ''Superstrings with spontaneously broken supersymmetry and their effective theories'', Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 318, 1989, pp.&nbsp;75–105 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(89)90048-5}} (over 350 citations)
*with J. P. Derendinger, S. Ferrara, F. Zwirner: ''On loop corrections to string effective field theories: field-dependent gauge couplings and σ-model anomalies'', Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 372, 1992, pp.&nbsp;145–188 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(92)90315-3}} (over 400 citations)
*with S. Ferrara, F. Zwirner: ''Mass formulae and natural hierarchy in string effective supergravities'', Nucl. Phys. B, vol. 429, 1994, pp.&nbsp;589–625 {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(94)90154-6}}
*with  Nicolaos Toumbas: ''Aspects of String Cosmology'', Corfu Summer Institute 2012, [https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.2809 arxiv.org preprint]
